caption:
Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: bpm is 68. key is D minor, and scale is minor. Emotional Piano-and-Strings Ballad, a father's steady reassurance over a slow, warm, cinematic pulse.
Global Emotional Progression: The track opens on a single piano chord and a far-off rain bed, the male lead quiet and close, admitting the day has been too loud. The verses stay sparse, piano and a low pad only, letting the thoughts run without pushing them. The pre-chorus is the first lift, cellos entering under the voice on the line about spinning the thread back in. The chorus opens gently rather than in a rush: a soft kick and brushed snare, a low string bed, and a male harmony a third beneath the lead that makes the admission feel shared. The second verse moves to a small acoustic guitar and the sound of a glass set down, the most domestic passage on the record. The instrumental is sixteen bars of solo piano over held strings, with no drums. The bridge falls back to voice and piano, nearly spoken, then builds through the last two lines as the strings return. The final chorus is full and warm, the choir pad rising on the line about being a quiet place, and the post-chorus strips the drums again. The outro is a single piano and voice, decaying into room tone.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: A rainy window at dusk, a child's glass of water set on a sill, a kitchen with the lights low, a car park after a bad meeting, a hallway full of the day's noise going quiet, a loving father and daughter montage.
Sonics & Production Profile: Close, warm, small-room soundstage with the vocal forward and almost unprocessed. Natural acoustic polish: woody low end from upright bass and piano rather than synthetic sub-bass, generous midrange left intact, soft unhyped top end. Dynamics stay low and conversational in the verses and open gently rather than loudly in the choruses. Light room reverb on the instruments, with the lead vocal kept close and dry so every breath and consonant reads.

Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Singer A (Male). A warm, lived-in baritone in his late thirties, unhurried and close to the microphone in the low register, opening into a grainier and slightly frayed tone as he lifts into his upper chest voice.
Vocal Style: Confiding and nearly spoken in the verses, sitting right on the microphone with audible breath and soft consonants, as though the song is being said to one person rather than performed. The pre-chorus tightens the phrasing and lifts in pitch. The chorus is open-throated and plain, carried on feeling rather than power, with the catch left in the voice instead of smoothed away. The bridge falls back almost to speech before the final build.
Harmony/Backing Vocals: A single low male harmony a third beneath the lead thickens each chorus. A soft wordless pad of female and child-register voices joins the final chorus for warmth and height. Airy unison doubles of the lead drift beneath the outro.
Vocal FX: Close and dry lead with a short plate reverb and no audible delay through the verses. A gentle slapback opens on the choruses. The outro vocal is washed in a long soft reverb tail that decays into the room sound.

Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: Warm upright piano carries the whole song from the first chord to the final decay, and a low string bed holds beneath every chorus. Secondary: Cellos enter with the pre-chorus; a soft choir pad and a brass bed widen the final chorus; a single acoustic guitar colours the second verse only. Groove & Foundation Progression: No percussion in the intro or the verses. A brushed snare and soft kick enter with the chorus, leave for the instrumental and the bridge, and return at full weight for the final chorus. Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: Distant rain, a glass set down on wood, a single sustained string note under the last line of each verse, and a long piano decay that ends the record.
lyrics:
[intro]
Some days start with thunder
Before the sun is high,
A hundred voices asking
And no good way to reply.

[verse]
The phone goes off at seven with a problem I can't name,
The traffic sits and doesn't move and then it moves again.
There's a man who wants an answer and a number that won't close,
And a meeting in an hour where I'll say that it's all fine.
I keep a face for all of it, I've worn it till it fits,
I can carry a whole bad week and never let it slip.
Then I come in through the front door, drop my bag against the wall,
And there's music in the kitchen and you dancing in the hall.
You don't stop to look at me, you're too far into the song,
You just reach out for my hand and pull me where you are.

[pre-chorus]
You don't ask me how it went,
You don't need the whole report,
You just take my hand and spin me
Till I've lost the thread of it.

[chorus]
When the world gets loud,
You're the quiet I come back to.
When I can't hear myself,
I just stand here and I watch you.
You don't fix a single thing,
You don't know there's any weight,
You just put your hand in mine
And the shouting goes away.

[verse]
You brought a flower in to me from somewhere near the fence,
The stem was bent, the petals torn, it didn't make much sense.
You said that it was only tired and wanted somewhere small,
So we filled a glass with water and we set it by the wall.
You checked on it at bedtime and you checked on it at dawn,
You turned it to the window so it knew which way was warm.
By Thursday it was standing and you never said a thing,
You just carried on with breakfast like it's normal to be mending.
I have spent my whole life hammering at problems till they break,
And you fixed a broken flower with a glass and three days' faith.

[pre-chorus]
You don't ask me how it went,
You don't need the whole report,
You just take my hand and spin me
Till I've lost the thread of it.

[chorus]
When the world gets loud,
You're the quiet I come back to.
When I can't hear myself,
I just stand here and I watch you.
You don't fix a single thing,
You don't know there's any weight,
You just put your hand in mine
And the shouting goes away.

[instrumental]

[bridge]
I don't know how to tell you
That the thing you do is rare,
That there are grown men twice your size
Who have never learned to care
The way you cared about a flower
With a stem that wouldn't hold.
So if anybody ever says
Your softness makes you small,
They have never been the broken thing
You carried down the hall.
They have never been the tired man
You turned towards the sun.

[chorus]
When the world gets loud,
You're the quiet I come back to.
When I can't hear myself,
I just stand here and I watch you.
I came here to be the shelter,
To stand between you and the rain,
And you've been the one who's quietly
Been taking it away.

[post-chorus]
The world can keep on shouting,
The night can rise and fall,
There's a glass beside the window
And you dancing in the hall.

[outro]
So let it all get louder,
Let the thunder do its worst.
There's a flower on the windowsill
And it is standing up.
So let the phone keep ringing,
Let the traffic have its say,
I've got a little hand to hold
And a whole hall left to play.
